title: Yoko Ono: Music of the Mind
description: Yoko Ono: Music of the Mind traces more than seven decades of Yoko Ono's groundbreaking career, from her early text-based works in the 1950s and '60s to recent large-scale installations informed by her ongoing campaigns for world peace. Organized in collaboration with Tate Modern, London, the exhibition—Ono's first solo museum exhibition in Southern California—explores her radical approach to art, language, and participation, challenging conventional ideas about the roles of artist and audience. Throughout the exhibition, Ono's celebrated "instruction" pieces invite you to become a part of the art itself. Tie a wish to an olive tree. Hammer a nail into a painting. title: Suddenly, Last Summer Double Feature: Presented by Dirty Looks
description: tickets The gayest movie ever made! Elizabeth Taylor is locked up in a mental hospital. Katherine Hepburn is Violet, the New Orleans aristocrat willing to sign any check to silence her. Montgomery Clift is Dr. Sugar, a surgeon popularizing the lobotomy. The heart of this sick triangle is deceased poet and sex tourist, Sebastian. Every fevered monologue was put to page by Tennessee Williams. Oh, and throw in Mercedes McCambridge, the lesbian antagonist of Johnny Guitar and voice of Regan in The Exorcist, just for good measure. Fifty years in the heat of this wily romp, John Aes-Nihil directed a video remake, starring Vaginal Davis, Jade Gordon, Bibbe Hanson, Jason Majik, Lance Loud and Goddess Bunny. title: The Legend of Leigh Bowery
description: Tickets In this documentary feature, Charles Atlas examines the legend and the life of his friend and collaborator – artist, performer, fashion designer, model, and club promoter and icon Leigh Bowery. In a remarkable and brief period before his early death from AIDS-related illness in 1994, Bowery made an indelible mark on nightlife, fashion, and artmaking in London, New York, and beyond. Through a wealth of archival footage and frank and uncensored interviews with friends, family, and fellow artists, Atlas traces the extraordinary impact Bowery had on culture, recalling his infamous nightclub Taboo, his collaborations with dancer and choreographer Michael Clark, his time as a muse to Lucien Freud, and his notorious, innovative, and influential fashions and performances. title: The Lure
description: Tickets The Lure is a 2015 Polish musical horror film directed by Agnieszka Smoczyńska and written by Robert Bolesto. This genre-defying horror-musical mash-up—the bold debut of Polish director Agnieszka Smoczyńska—follows a pair of carnivorous mermaid sisters drawn ashore to explore life on land in an alternate 1980s Poland. Their tantalizing siren songs and otherworldly auras make them overnight sensations as nightclub singers in the half-glam, half-decrepit world of Smoczyńska’s imagining. The director gives fierce teeth to her viscerally sensual, darkly feminist twist on Hans Christian Andersen’s “The Little Mermaid,” in which the girls’ bond is tested and their survival threatened after one sister falls for a human. title: Haruko Tanaka + Reader Chorus documentary
description: Tickets Haruko Tanaka (b. Queens, NY, 1974; d. October 2019) was a Los Angeles–based artist, photographer, graphic designer, and filmmaker engaged in social practice. Born in the United States, she was raised in England and Japan. Tanaka earned a B.A. in Fine Art from the University of Southern California in 1997 and an M.F.A. in Photography and Media Art from the California Institute of the Arts in 2003. Her visual work was exhibited widely at venues such as the Library Foundation of Los Angeles, the Japanese American National Museum, the Museum of Modern Art, CUE Art Foundation, the Torrance Art Museum, and the Armory Center for the Arts. She also screened her films internationally, including at the Rotterdam International Film Festival and the Asian American International Film Festival.

title: Evidence by Anne Schmitt
description: Tickets The following description was written by Anne Schmitt: Evidence is both an analysis of corporate spending and the impact of dark money on US politics and ideology and a personal meditation on ideas of family and care. The film is a meditation on the intersection of American politics, ideas of family, and the right wing’s intentional assault on bodily autonomy. This is my fourth feature; each an examination of ideology and its construction in the United States. This film is by far my most personal work and attempts to understand how my own family (or birth and of choice) was sculpted within a mythology of capitalism. description: Cinema Under Pressure is a Monday night film series at The Wende Museum. It explores the struggles over what audiences are permitted to see. Each screening is paired with a discussion featuring a guest expert. This month’s film is The Life and Death of Colonel Blimp (1943), written, produced, and directed by Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger. The story follows British officer Clive Candy across forty years of war, peace, and love. His closest friend is a German officer. Winston Churchill learned of the production in 1942 and asked his ministers to find a way to stop it. The War Office refused to lend the filmmakers military support. By turns mesmerizing and unsettling, KAMIKAZE HEARTS is both a fascinating record of pre-gentrification San Francisco’s X-rated underground and an intense, searing love story. title: Racist by Design: Kelly Lytle Hernández in Conversation
description: Kelly Lytle Hernández launches her new book Racist by Desig n in conversation with Los Angeles Times columnist Jean Guerrero. The book traces the American immigration system from its origins to the way it works today. Most accounts begin with the Chinese Exclusion Act of the late nineteenth century. Lytle Hernández starts a full century earlier, with the Haitian Revolution of the 1790s, which prompted both the country’s first immigration bans and its first refugee resettlement program. She shows how eugenicists and Jim Crow segregationists built much of the current system as expressly whites only, and how Congress amended that system during the Civil Rights Movement while leaving many of its rules intact. Navigating Our Media Ecosystem: Reclaiming Our Stories & Media
description: The stories we hear and see shape the world we live in. During these two free hands-on workshops, we will explore our relationships with media, technology, and popular culture. We will analyze media and create our own alternative messages with a focus on the ways environmental and climate justice impact our health. These events are free for everyone. We are all part of a media ecosystem, whether we’re on social media, watching YouTube, reading articles, or sharing links with our friends and family. We will explore tools for critical media literacy and – as a community- discover how we can tell our own stories and create our own media. title: The Bengali: An Evening of Film and the Power of Storytelling
description: Join us for an evening of film, conversation, and community at the Wende Museum as we explore the stories we inherit, the identities we carry, and the unexpected connections that shape our world. In The Bengali, named one of Nonfics’ Top 20 Documentaries, director Kavery Kaul takes an American woman to India to uncover the past of her grandfather, Shaik Mohamed Musa. He was one of the early group of men who arrived in the late nineteenth century and married African-American women. Her unlikely quest triggers a boldly different encounter between East and West. A personal search becomes a deeper journey into culture, memory, and identity, breaking barriers and building bridges, revealing how histories travel, and families form across unexpected places.
